title: Part One, Chapter 5: The Two Boys against Vucub-caquix and His Sons

verses.t: This is, or was, the cause of the destruction of Vucub-caquix by the two boys: Hun-ahpu, as one was called (a hunter), and the other called Xbalanque (a diminutive of jaguar and deer). These too were gods, and so that pride seemed wrong to them, because he displayed it before the Heart of the Sky. And the two boys said, "It will not be good for this to go on, for then men will not be able to live here on the earth. So we shall try to shoot him with the blowgun while he eats; we shall shoot him and give him a sickness, and then his riches, his precious stones and his jades, by which he makes himself great, will come to an end. And so it shall be for all men: no one is to make himself great because he has riches," said the two boys, each with his blowgun on his shoulder. Now this Vucub-caquix had two sons: the first was called Sipacua and the second Cabracan, and their mother was called Chimalmat, the wife of Vucub-caquix. And this son Sipacua fed and lived upon the great mountains; besides this, in a single night the mountains called Hun-ahpu-pecul, Yaxcanul-mucamob and Hulisnab appeared already made, for in one night Sipacua would make a mountain. And his brother Cabracan (that is, "of two feet") shook the mountains, great and small, and made them tremble. And so these two sons of Vucub-caquix also grew proud. And Vucub-caquix said, "Know that I am the sun." "And I am the maker of the earth," said Sipacua. "And I," said Cabracan, "am the one who moves the earth; I shall throw down the whole earth." And so the sons of Vucub-caquix grew proud as well, through their father's pride. And this seemed very wrong to the two boys, Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque; and our first fathers and mothers had not yet been made. And so the two boys planned the deaths of Vucub-caquix, Sipacua and Cabracan.
